# Jira

This plugin for the `compliance-framework` evaluates Jira and Jira Service Management (JSM) data to ensure Change Request processes are properly followed prior to new deployments.

This page is for **operators** who run the `plugin-jira` plugin with the CCF Agent, and for **developers** who write policies for it. It documents [v0.2.5](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-jira/releases/tag/v0.2.5) and is generated from the plugin's [README at v0.2.5](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-jira/blob/v0.2.5/README.md).

## How it works

### Usage

The plugin implements the `Runner` interface and is executed by the compliance agent.

```bash
# Example execution (internal to framework)
./plugin-jira --config config.json
```

## Requirements

### Setup Instructions

#### 1. Authentication Setup

The plugin supports two authentication methods:

##### Option A: Service Account + OAuth2 (Recommended for Cloud)
This method uses Jira's [OAuth 2.0 (3LO) for apps](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/oauth-2-3lo-apps/) or more specifically, for service-to-service integrations, you typically use [API Tokens with a Service Account](https://support.atlassian.com/atlassian-account/docs/manage-api-tokens-for-your-atlassian-account/) or [OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/oauth-2-client-credentials-apps/) (if available for your organization).

**How to set up a Service Account:**
1. Create a dedicated Atlassian account (e.g., `compliance-bot@yourcompany.com`).
2. Invite this account to your Jira instance.
3. Follow Atlassian's guide on [Service Accounts](https://support.atlassian.com/organization-administration/docs/use-service-accounts/).

##### Option B: API Token (Fallback)
1. Log in to Jira as the Service Account.
2. Go to **Account Settings > Security > API Tokens**.
3. Create a new API token and save it securely.

#### 2. Minimal Permissions (Scopes)

The Service Account needs the following minimal permissions to collect compliance data:

- **Global Permissions**:
    - `Browse Users` (to see approvers and authors)
- **Project Permissions (for all target projects)**:
    - `Browse Projects`
    - `View Development Tools` (for Software API dev links)
    - `Administer Projects` (optional, for detailed workflow/scheme inspection)
- **OAuth Scopes (Cloud)**:
    - `read:jira-work`
    - `read:jira-user`
    - `read:servicedesk-request`
    - `manage:jira-configuration` (for workflows and schemes)

## Configuration

The plugin is configured via the `PluginConfig` structure:

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `base_url` | The URL of your Jira instance (e.g., `https://your-domain.atlassian.net`) |
| `auth_type` | `oauth2` or `token` |
| `client_id` | OAuth2 Client ID (for `oauth2` auth) |
| `client_secret` | OAuth2 Client Secret (for `oauth2` auth) |
| `api_token` | API Token (for `token` auth) |
| `user_email` | Service Account email (for `token` auth) |
| `project_keys` | Comma-separated list of Project Keys to monitor |
| `policy_labels` | JSON map of labels to attach to generated evidence |

### Policy data

Any `policy_data` set on this plugin's block in the agent configuration is passed
to every policy evaluation and is available to Rego as `data.<key>`. Which keys
are read depends on the policy bundle; for example:

```yaml
plugins:
  jira:
    # ...source, policies and config as usual...
    policy_data:
      approver_groups:
        - change-advisory-board
```

## Evidence collected

### Features

- **Authentication**: Supports OAuth2 (2-Legged OAuth / Client Credentials) and API Tokens.
- **Data Collection**:
    - **Jira Platform**: Projects, Workflows, Schemes, Issue Types, Custom Fields, Audit Records, and Permissions.
    - **Jira Service Management**: Native Approvals and SLAs.
    - **Jira Software**: Development Information (GitHub PRs/commits) and Deployment events.
- **Policy Evaluation**: Integration with OPA policies to calculate compliance evidence based on collected Jira metadata.

## Policy input

The plugin evaluates one kind of resource, a Jira project, and a policy receives one document per project as `input`. The document always has a `projects` array with exactly one entry, the project being evaluated, next to the Jira-wide `global_permissions` and `audit_records`, which are the same for every project. Fields are listed by their path inside the document; a field marked as left out is missing from the document, not null, so test for it with `object.get` or a default. Only open issues are included (status category `To Do` or `In Progress`, or no status category), and only for the issue types the plugin searches for, which are set by `change_request_issue_types` (`Change Request` and `Change` by default). Projects can be limited with `project_keys`. Reads that fail are logged and skipped, so any of the lists can also be missing because Jira did not return it.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `projects` | array of objects | One entry, the project being evaluated. The fields below are inside it. |
| `projects[].project` | object | The Jira project. |
| `projects[].project.id` | string | Numeric ID of the project, as a string. |
| `projects[].project.key` | string | Project key, for example `PAY`. |
| `projects[].project.name` | string | Project display name. |
| `projects[].project.self` | string | API URL of the project. Left out when empty. |
| `projects[].project.description` | string | Project description. Left out when empty. |
| `projects[].project.style` | string | `classic` or `next-gen`. Left out when empty. |
| `projects[].project.simplified` | boolean | True for a team-managed project. Left out when false. |
| `projects[].project.projectCategory` | object | Category of the project, with `id`, `name`, `description` and `self`. Left out when the project has no category. |
| `projects[].project.insight` | object | Activity summary, with `totalIssueCount` and `lastIssueUpdateTime`. Left out when Jira returns none. |
| `projects[].project.lead` | object | The project lead, a user object (see user below). Left out when Jira returns none. |
| `projects[].project.components` | array of objects | Project components, each with `id`, `name`, `description`, `self`, `assignee`, `assigneeType`, `project` and `projectId`. Left out when none. |
| `projects[].project.issueTypes` | array of objects | Issue types Jira lists on the project, each with `id` and `name`. Left out when none. |
| `projects[].workflow_schemes` | array of objects | Workflow schemes associated with the project. Left out when none. |
| `projects[].workflow_schemes[].id` | integer | Scheme ID. |
| `projects[].workflow_schemes[].name` | string | Scheme name. |
| `projects[].workflow_schemes[].description` | string | Scheme description. Left out when empty. |
| `projects[].workflow_schemes[].defaultWorkflow` | string | Name of the default workflow. Left out when empty. |
| `projects[].workflow_schemes[].issueTypeMappings` | object (string to string) | Issue type to workflow name. Left out when empty. |
| `projects[].workflow_schemes[].draft` | boolean | True for a draft scheme. Left out when false. |
| `projects[].workflow_schemes[].self` | string | API URL of the scheme. Left out when empty. |
| `projects[].workflows` | array of objects | Workflows the project's issues use, found through its workflow schemes, or by name or scope when it has no scheme. Left out when none. |
| `projects[].workflows[].id` | string | Workflow ID. |
| `projects[].workflows[].name` | string | Workflow name. |
| `projects[].workflows[].description` | string | Workflow description. Left out when empty. |
| `projects[].workflows[].scope` | object | Where the workflow applies: `type` (`GLOBAL` or `PROJECT`) and, for a project-scoped workflow, `project`. |
| `projects[].workflows[].version` | object | Workflow version, with `id` and `versionNumber`. |
| `projects[].workflows[].isEditable` | boolean | Whether the workflow can be edited. Left out when false. |
| `projects[].workflows[].published` | boolean | Whether the workflow is published. Left out when false. |
| `projects[].workflows[].created` | string | Creation time as Jira reports it. Left out when empty. |
| `projects[].workflows[].modified` | string | Last modification time as Jira reports it. Left out when empty. |
| `projects[].workflows[].statuses` | array of objects | Statuses in the workflow. Left out when none. Each has the fields below. |
| `projects[].workflows[].statuses[].id` | string | Status ID. |
| `projects[].workflows[].statuses[].name` | string | Status name. |
| `projects[].workflows[].statuses[].statusReference` | string | Reference that ties the status to the global status. |
| `projects[].workflows[].statuses[].statusCategory` | string | Status category, for example `TODO`, `IN_PROGRESS` or `DONE`. Left out when empty. |
| `projects[].workflows[].statuses[].approvalConfiguration` | object | Approval rule on the status: `active`, `conditionType` (`number`, `percent` or `numberPerPrincipal`), `conditionValue`, `fieldId`, `transitionApproved`, `transitionRejected`, and optionally `exclude` and `prePopulatedFieldId`. Left out when the status needs no approval. |
| `projects[].workflows[].transitions` | array of objects | Transitions in the workflow. Left out when none. Each has the fields below. |
| `projects[].workflows[].transitions[].id` | string | Transition ID. |
| `projects[].workflows[].transitions[].name` | string | Transition name. |
| `projects[].workflows[].transitions[].toStatusReference` | string | Status the transition leads to. Left out when empty. |
| `projects[].workflows[].transitions[].fromStatus` | array of strings | Status references the transition starts from. Left out when none. |
| `projects[].workflows[].transitions[].type` | string | Transition type, for example `DIRECTED`. Left out when empty. |
| `projects[].workflows[].transitions[].isConditional` | boolean | True when the transition has conditions. Left out when false. |
| `projects[].issues` | array of objects | Open change request issues of the project. Left out when there are none. |
| `projects[].issues[].key` | string | Issue key, for example `PAY-142`. |
| `projects[].issues[].fields` | object | The issue's fields as Jira returns them, keyed by field ID, such as `summary`, `status`, `issuetype`, `project`, `assignee` and any custom field. |
| `projects[].issues[].fields_with_metadata` | array of objects | The same fields with their definition: `id`, `name`, `type`, `custom` and `value`. Left out when empty. |
| `projects[].issues[].changelog` | object or null | Change history: `histories`, `startAt`, `maxResults` and `total`. Each history has `author`, `created` (RFC 3339) and `items` with `field`, `fromString` and `toString`. Null when no changelog was fetched. |
| `projects[].issues[].approvals` | array of objects | Service Management approvals on the issue. Left out when none. |
| `projects[].issues[].approvals[].id` | string | Approval ID. |
| `projects[].issues[].approvals[].name` | string | Approval name. Left out when empty. |
| `projects[].issues[].approvals[].finalDecision` | string | `approved`, `declined` or `pending`. Left out when empty. |
| `projects[].issues[].approvals[].canAnswerApproval` | boolean | Whether the calling account can answer the approval. Left out when false. |
| `projects[].issues[].approvals[].approvers` | array of objects | Each approver is an object with `approver` (a user object) and `approverDecision`, left out when empty. |
| `projects[].issues[].approvals[].createdDate` | object | When the approval was created, with `epochMillis`, `friendly`, `iso8601` and `jira`. Each is left out when empty. |
| `projects[].issues[].approvals[].completedDate` | object | When the approval was completed, with the same fields as `createdDate`. |
| `projects[].issues[].slas` | array of objects | Service Management SLAs on the issue. Left out when none. |
| `projects[].issues[].slas[].id` | string | SLA ID. |
| `projects[].issues[].slas[].name` | string | SLA name. |
| `projects[].issues[].slas[].state` | string | `MET`, `BREACHED` or `IN_PROGRESS`. |
| `projects[].issues[].slas[].completedCycles` | array of objects | Finished SLA cycles. Left out when none. |
| `projects[].issues[].slas[].ongoingCycle` | object | The running cycle. Left out when there is none. Cycles have `breached`, `withinCalendar` and the times `startTime`, `stopTime`, `breachTime`, `elapsedTime`, `remainingTime` and `goalDuration`, each with `friendly`, `millis`, `jira` and `iso8601`. |
| `projects[].issues[].dev_info` | object | Linked development data. Left out when none was found. |
| `projects[].issues[].dev_info.pull_requests` | array of objects | Pull requests linked to the issue, each with `id`, `status` and `url`. |
| `projects[].issues[].deployments` | array of objects | Deployments linked to the issue, each with `id`, `environment`, `status` and `timestamp` (RFC 3339). Left out when none. |
| `projects[].issue_types` | array of objects | Issue types used by the project's issues, each with `id` and `name`. Left out when none. |
| `projects[].fields` | array of objects | Field definitions matching the fields of the project's issues, each with `id`, `name` and `schema`. Left out when none. |
| `projects[].statuses` | array of objects | Statuses the project's issues are in, each with `id`, `name`, `scope`, and optionally `description`, `statusCategory`, `statusReference`, `iconUrl` and `self`. Left out when none. |
| `global_permissions` | array of objects | Global permissions of the account the plugin uses, each with `key`, `name`, `description` and `type`. Left out when none. |
| `audit_records` | array of objects | Jira audit log records. Left out when none. |
| `audit_records[].id` | integer | Record ID. |
| `audit_records[].summary` | string | What happened. |
| `audit_records[].created` | string (RFC 3339 time) | When it happened. Null when Jira gives no time. |
| `audit_records[].category` | string | Audit category. |
| `audit_records[].authorAccountId` | string | Account that made the change. Left out when empty. |
| `audit_records[].authorKey` | string | Legacy user key of the author. Left out when empty. |
| `audit_records[].description` | string | Longer description. Left out when empty. |
| `audit_records[].eventSource` | string | Where the change came from. Left out when empty. |
| `audit_records[].remoteAddress` | string | IP address of the author. Left out when empty. |
| `audit_records[].objectItem` | object | The object changed, with `id`, `name`, `typeName`, `parentId` and `parentName`. Left out when none. |
| `audit_records[].associatedItems` | array of objects | Related objects, with the same fields as `objectItem`. Left out when none. |
| `audit_records[].changedValues` | array of objects | Changes made, each with `fieldName`, `changedFrom` and `changedTo`. Left out when none. |

An example input:

## Subject templates

The subject templates this plugin registers. Each example is built from sample data.

### jira-project

A Jira project. Title: `Jira Project: {{ .project_key }}`. The evidence also carries `provider` (`jira`), `project_name` and `jira_url` labels, which are not part of the identity.

| Identity key | Description |
|---|---|
| `project_key` | The unique key of the Jira project, for example `PAY`. |

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "jira-project",
  "type": "component",
  "title": "Jira Project: PAY",
  "description": "Jira project Payments Platform (PAY)",
  "purpose": "Represents a Jira project being monitored for compliance",
  "identityLabels": {
    "project_key": "PAY"
  }
}
```
